items.summary: A provenance-bound values model published as a public evaluator rather than deployed as a filter — why open weights defeat a filter and strengthen a referee, why the same weights bear three different relations to the model they judge, and why an evaluator that gatekeeps its own judgments has reproduced the defect it exists to correct. A values model — a model that judges conduct against a standard — is an established artifact. Guard models, safety classifiers, critic models, preference models and process reward models all instantiate the family, and the engineering is not in dispute. What is in dispute, and what this paper specifies, is the posture in which such an artifact is published , which we argue is not a deployment detail but the property that determines whether the artifact does anything at all. We state an inversion as a design principle. A values model deployed as a filter — sitting in a serving path, permitting or refusing — is defeated by publication of its weights, because the published artifact is precisely the oracle against which an attacker optimizes; a staged black-box attack (STACK) reaches roughly 71% success against a defended classifier pipeline that had held earlier attacks near zero, and an attacker holding the weights has strictly more than that attack needed. The same model published as an evaluator — emitting verdicts about systems it does not control — is not defeated by publication, and its positive findings are strengthened by it, because open weights are what allow a third party to reproduce and therefore to trust its verdicts. The same openness hands the judged party an optimization target, and §4.1 states what that concedes: a clean or empty result from an open referee proves less against an adaptive party than the first draft of this paper allowed. Openness is not a property with a fixed sign. Its sign is set by posture, and in the referee posture it is mixed. From this we derive a second result. The independent-evaluation literature documents at length the ways in which the evaluated party's control over access corrupts evaluation: short access windows, low rate limits, evaluator dependence on the goodwill and funding of the party being evaluated. We observe that the defect is symmetric and that, in the work surveyed in §2, its mirror image has not been named. An evaluator that controls access to its own judgments holds the same kind of power, pointed the other way — it can decline to evaluate, deprioritize, or be unavailable for a party it wishes to spare or to punish. We therefore specify a non-gatekeeping constraint : the ability to obtain a judgment must not depend on the evaluator's permission, which requires that the model, the harness, and the evaluation corpus be freely runnable, and which makes any hosted endpoint a convenience rather than a channel. We specify provenance-binding as the constitutive constraint on the model's outputs: every judgment must resolve to a citation into a fixed canonical corpus, and a judgment that cannot be so resolved is withheld rather than emitted. This trades coverage for auditability deliberately, and it distinguishes the artifact from values models trained on preference data whose sources cannot be named, and from purpose-authored value-rule corpora, whose rules are written for the alignment task itself and therefore cannot serve as an independent ground truth. Finally we specify that a single such artifact bears three non-interchangeable relations to the systems it judges, selected by carrier: a gate in the publisher's own hardware, a citation requirement without veto in an autonomous successor agent, and a referee in the wider world. We state plainly that the middle case must not be implemented as the first, because a veto held by a smaller model over a more capable agent bounds that agent at the evaluator's ceiling — the weak-supervisor problem applied to the very system the arrangement exists to enable. items.summary: Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) is a fundamental inverse problem in geophysics to estimate subsurface properties, such as velocity, from seismic measurements. Recently, self-supervised learning methods remove the need for ground-truth velocity maps during training by leveraging a forward operator to simulate seismic data from predictions and backpropagate the gradients of reconstruction loss through it. In this work, we consider a more challenging setting without accessing such gradients. To this end, we incorporate reinforcement learning into self-supervised FWI and propose a framework named DeepWaveRL. Specifically, we reformulate FWI as a policy learning problem, where the policy network predicts velocity maps as actions, and a forward operator is used solely for simulation. A global scalar reward is computed based on data misfit for each prediction and used to weight policy gradients. Thus, learning proceeds without accessing the gradients from the forward operator. Given the indirect and coarse supervision signals, we further identify key strategies to stabilize learning and mitigate the spatial credit assignment bottleneck. Experimental results show that, despite relying entirely on a single scalar reward, DeepWaveRL achieves competitive performance compared to supervised and self-supervised baselines. These findings suggest that our framework offers a flexible and complementary learning paradigm for the FWI research community.
items.title: DeepWaveRL: Self-Supervised Full Waveform Inversion via Reinforcement Learning

items.summary: Reduced-order models (ROMs) learned from trusted numerical simulations enable the real-time simulation of complex physical systems, making computationally prohibitive tasks-such as uncertainty quantification and optimal control-tractable. In particular, data-driven ROMs are opening the opportunity to learn from both numerical simulations and experimental data. However, integrating these sources of information is far from straightforward. Real-world measurements often involve multiple sources of uncertainty, including non-Gaussian noise, latent heterogeneities, unknown or hidden system parameters, and multiscale phenomena occurring below the resolution of the data. Consequently, real-world data are better described by parametrized stochastic partial differential equations, for which the development of effective ROMs remains relatively unexplored. In this work, we introduce POD-CNF, a data-driven generative ROM for efficient uncertainty quantification of parametrized high-dimensional systems. The approach combines projection-based model reduction and deep generative modeling. First, Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is employed to obtain a low-dimensional representation of the solution manifold. A Conditional Normalizing Flow (CNF) is then trained to approximate the density of the reduced coefficients conditionally on the input parameters. This formulation allows the surrogate to capture complex, multimodal output distributions, going beyond standard regression-based ROMs and least-squares predictions. We assess the effectiveness of POD-CNF through numerical experiments, demonstrating its ability to accurately reproduce output distributions while substantially reducing computational costs. Finally, a proof-of-concept application illustrates how the generative paradigm facilitates integration into Bayesian inverse problems, highlighting promising directions for future research.
items.title: POD-CNF: reduced order modeling of parametrized stochastic PDEs via normalizing flows and proper orthogonal decomposition

items.summary: The self-controlled case series (SCCS) design is widely used in studies of rare events, for example of vaccine side effects. Conceptually, the design has two main features. First, it requires only data from individuals who have experienced the event of interest. Therefore, the design is especially useful when the outcome is rare and the available data come from surveillance or clinical records, say, of hospitalized patients. Second, because comparisons are made within single individuals, time-invariant confounding between treatment and outcome is eliminated. We formulate a set of sufficient identification assumptions for estimating the causal effect of vaccination on an adverse outcome under the SCCS design, drawing on ideas from the causal inference literature. Unlike the existing SCCS literature, we do not consider a parametric model as the starting point. This allows us to establish when and why the SCCS design allows identification of causal effects, using data from cases only. However, because the sufficient identifiability assumptions are implausible in some applications, we also develop statistical tests for the existence of a treatment effect that remain valid when only a subset of the identification assumptions holds.
items.title: Causal Inference from Self-controlled Case Series

items.summary: Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. We split this spectral shift into an operator channel and a frequency channel, each with a dimensionless measure. ST-GFM (Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting Model) filters every input step with Chebyshev and bidirectional diffusion filters on one learned, non-symmetric operator and alternates them with per-node temporal attention. For the operator channel we prove Frobenius-norm perturbation bounds for both graph branches, show that the Chebyshev bound is attained to first order, and compute its constant from the trained weights and the measured operator norm: 17.9 on METR-LA and 21.5 on PEMS-BAY. Under random edge dropout the trained layer moves by 2.0% to 3.1% of this bound. Masked Spectral Reconstruction (MSR), a self-supervised loss active in the first 40 epochs, matches the log power spectrum of the encoder output to that of the input. For small log-spectral residuals on unclamped bins it is proportional to an Itakura-Saito divergence to leading order. Removing it raises the 60-minute MAE by 0.30 on METR-LA, close to the 0.33 lost when all three self-supervised losses go. Under one shared evaluation pipeline, the 60-minute MAE of ST-GFM is 3.5% below a retrained STAEformer on METR-LA and 13.0% below it on PEMS-BAY. Its 60-minute MAE is 3.0980.017 on METR-LA (five seeds) and 1.5760.006 on PEMS-BAY (three seeds), the lowest PEMS-BAY MAE among twelve published baselines.
items.title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction

items.summary: This paper studies bidirectional pedestrian flow on a cyclic network of corridors. Each corridor consists of two lanes, while pedestrians may enter or leave the network at junctions. The dynamics are based on a 1-D, bidirectional, two-lane Lighthill-Whitham-Richards-type model, in which lane changes are described through explicit, density-dependent transfer rates that favor motion toward the less congested lane. We propose a localized lane-guidance control input that biases lane-changing behavior without creating pedestrians or reversing their walking direction. Such guidance may represent, for example, recommendations provided by staff or information screens. Under meaningful assumptions on the external inflows, we prove the existence and uniqueness of an admissible uniform equilibrium. We then linearize the system around this equilibrium and study the placement of localized guidance zones through a spectral detectability condition. We prove that, for any prescribed decay rate, two guidance patches located in a single, suitably chosen corridor are sufficient to satisfy the spectral detectability condition for all critical adjoint eigenmodes. This condition is necessary for the exponential stabilizability of the linearized system. Numerical experiments illustrate the spectral properties of the model and study the robustness of the modal observability condition with respect to the geometry and distribution of the guidance patches.
items.title: Localized Lane Guidance for a Bidirectional Pedestrian Cyclic Corridor: Equilibria and Generic Actuator Placement

items.summary: Recovering a 3D full-body human bone rig, which is used to animate a Computer-Generated Image (CGI) model is a challenging problem with many applications although successfully addressed by the motion capture systems with actors with markers worn all over the body with special suit and multiple cameras . In this paper, we detail the bottom-up approach derived from Open Pose, winner of Common Objects in Context (COCO) 2016 KEYPOINTS Challenge, because of its decent qual ity and robustness of detection of multiple numbers of people in the frame with focus . Proposed network design and optimized post-processing with the full solution of video to 2D conversion run at acceptable speeds . The second part of 2D pose to 3D pose conversion u ses a novel Occlusion-Robust Pose-Maps (ORPM) which enables full body pose inference even under strong partial occlusions by other people and objects in the scene . O RPM outputs a fixed number of maps which encodes the 3D joint locations of all people in the scene . Body part associations allow us to infer 3D pose of arbitrary numbers of people without explicit bounding box prediction which increases performance of pose inference . The final combination of the two networks is where a single camera can detect human motion and display the 3D rep resentation in a three-dimensional space in real-time.  Provenance Note: Previously published in the Proceedings of the 3rd National Conference on Science, Engineering and Technology (SET Conference 2021) . Re-archived for public record due to the permanent closure of the original archive.

items.summary: A shibboleth economy is a cultural system in which the rewards of decoding, a fluency-gain reward, identity affirmation, collective affiliation, and positional rank, become self-sustaining, so that demand for distinction feeds back into cultural production and communicative opacity becomes value-bearing rather than merely costly. Cultural capital theory, from Bourdieu through the fan-studies lineage, explains why scarce decoding competence produces distinction; a shibboleth economy begins where that distinction becomes demand and the demand alters what gets made, through evolutionary selection on engagement rather than any calculating producer. The paper develops the loop and its consequences. A two-type model distinguishes lexical figuration, which maps represented features to meanings and is bootstrappable within a single work, from modal figuration, which maps the representational act itself to an ontological status and is stabilised only by shared representational infrastructure, of which canon is the most powerful form. In markets poor in effective codebook coverage, exemplified by industrial-era Hollywood, uncaught references are priced as lost customers and a self-teaching visual pidgin is selected, later mistaken for neutral realism; in codebook-rich markets the operating point moves to selective permeability, legible to the invested and closed to the casual, with the equilibrium set by the opposed pulls of affiliation and rank. Democratisation of a key causes migration and displacement rather than collapse; a hard cultural border is a boundary condition that slows depreciation and opens an export axis; and when demand for keys outruns authenticated supply, the predicted pathology is key inflation, defined as growth in the ratio of claimed authorised readings to verifiably authorised ones, driven by provenance laundering. Two model-implied expectations, codebook import markets and synthetic canon manufacture, are tested against known cases, with modal transfer breadth as the surviving strong claim, and three forward predictions are stated, led by key migration under democratisation.
items.title: The Shibboleth Economy

items.summary: Distribution feeders host managed electric vehicle charging through control loops, a site energy management system enforcing a connection-point limit and a demand response aggregator dispatching curtailment, that act on telemetry the charging stations report about themselves. An adversary controlling authorised but compromised reporting sources can move those loops without switching any physical load and without defeating any transport control. We define the undetected harm frontier, the greatest feeder harm reachable while raising no alarm under a given validation setup, and show that a bound on it exists only when at least one reference in the validation chain has provenance independent of the compromised source. We classify grid-edge telemetry into four provenance classes and evaluate seven validation setups on seven published distribution test systems by quasi-static time-series power flow, parameterised by measurements from a live OCPP 2.0.1 stack. Five of the seven setups, including textbook weighted-least-squares bad data detection, trace an identical frontier and constrain the adversary not at all. The two that bound the harm are exactly the two holding an independent measurement, which is the taxonomy's prediction. Under the unanchored setups the attack crosses the statutory voltage floor on IEEE 33-bus, crosses the conductor thermal rating on four of six networks robustly across random realisations, inflates apparent hosting capacity by 7.5 percent, and misallocates settlement. The mitigation this implies is not a better detector but the acquisition of one measurement the adversary does not produce.
items.title: False Data Injection from Authorized EV Chargers on Distribution Feeders

items.summary: The term "AI slop" is commonly treated as a property of the generator: text is slop because a model produced it. This paper argues that slop is a property of the process. It names generation that reached a reader without the review it needed, and reviewed generation is a draft, whoever generated it. On that account the slop critique is largely mitigable by review processes run with or by language models, but not on the grounds usually offered. The argument is not that models review better than they write, nor that they review better than humans. It is that one large class of faults, provenance, is invisible to a reading human at population scale and cheap for a machine to check: across four top-tier venues, papers carrying hallucinated citations received reviewer ratings indistinguishable from clean papers, accepted and rejected submissions whose ratings differed by two points carried the same share of them, and a venue-scale audit cost about four cents a paper (Russinovich, Siva Kumar and Salem 2026). Review is the better-suited task for a model for five structural reasons: a fixed target, a brief that says where to look, permission to answer "cannot verify", no stake in the document, and the generated text as a map of where to check. The remedy for slop is therefore a division of labour that assigns the provenance pass to the machine and the reasoning pass to the human. The paper names five mechanisms by which unreviewed generation acquires faults that are invisible from inside the text, carries four corrections as explicit limits, and reports one case in which two reviewers of different kind, a human on a phone and a model under a provenance brief, found disjoint error classes with no overlap, every provenance fault sitting on a source the generating model had not opened. The case is N = 1 and is offered as a specimen, not a result; the paper's own first draft supplies a second specimen, by the mechanism the paper describes. The division of labour is then placed under its binding constraint: when an AI agent is institutionally positioned as an employee, managers catch fewer errors themselves and pass the review on (Wiles, Hsu, Bedard and Kropp 2026), so the design must survive the effect it is meant to offset. Seven hypotheses are stated, each with the observation that would falsify it.
items.title: Slop Is a Process Property

items.summary: Classical creative-process orderings put divergence early and convergence late, and the Double Diamond formalises the rule twice over. This paper argues the ordering was never a law of cognition but a map of costs: divergence goes early because reopening a converged process has historically been ruinous, and the entire discipline of the framework exists to protect against that reopening. When drafting cost collapses by orders of magnitude, as it does when an author works with a language model as typewriter, the protected assumption dissolves and the optimal ordering inverts: converge first, then diverge, because a late horizon either restarts a now-cheap process or spawns a child concept from a sharpened parent. The paper's second claim types reviewer instances in multi-model chains by regression target rather than capability, and states the Hein Condition: a mode-regressing reviewer's yield is proportional to the sharpness of the artefact it receives, because the modal response to an unsharp artefact is the generic response, so the same instance is most fluent exactly where it is least useful. A slot theory follows, carnivore, auditor, mode-regressor, children, each reviewer placed where its failure mode is cheapest, and child viability rises with parent sharpness at spawn. The claims are exercised on a fully documented case: a five-pass, three-model review chain run on a single paper in a single day, with every absorption, declination, and provenance failure logged. Four predictions close, including that review chains are provenance systems measurable by the sibling paper's key-inflation ratio.

items.summary: A provenance-bound values model published as a public evaluator rather than deployed as a filter — why open weights defeat a filter and strengthen a referee, why the same weights bear three different relations to the model they judge, and why an evaluator that gatekeeps its own judgments has reproduced the defect it exists to correct. A values model — a model that judges conduct against a standard — is an established artifact. Guard models, safety classifiers, critic models, preference models and process reward models all instantiate the family, and the engineering is not in dispute. What is in dispute, and what this paper specifies, is the posture in which such an artifact is published , which we argue is not a deployment detail but the property that determines whether the artifact does anything at all. We state an inversion as a design principle. A values model deployed as a filter — sitting in a serving path, permitting or refusing — is defeated by publication of its weights, because the published artifact is precisely the oracle against which an attacker optimizes; a staged black-box attack (STACK) reaches roughly 71% success against a defended classifier pipeline that had held earlier attacks near zero, and an attacker holding the weights has strictly more than that attack needed. The same model published as an evaluator — emitting verdicts about systems it does not control — is not defeated by publication, and its positive findings are strengthened by it, because open weights are what allow a third party to reproduce and therefore to trust its verdicts. The same openness hands the judged party an optimization target, and §4.1 states what that concedes: a clean or empty result from an open referee proves less against an adaptive party than the first draft of this paper allowed. Openness is not a property with a fixed sign. Its sign is set by posture, and in the referee posture it is mixed. From this we derive a second result. The independent-evaluation literature documents at length the ways in which the evaluated party's control over access corrupts evaluation: short access windows, low rate limits, evaluator dependence on the goodwill and funding of the party being evaluated. We observe that the defect is symmetric and that, in the work surveyed in §2, its mirror image has not been named. An evaluator that controls access to its own judgments holds the same kind of power, pointed the other way — it can decline to evaluate, deprioritize, or be unavailable for a party it wishes to spare or to punish. We therefore specify a non-gatekeeping constraint : the ability to obtain a judgment must not depend on the evaluator's permission, which requires that the model, the harness, and the evaluation corpus be freely runnable, and which makes any hosted endpoint a convenience rather than a channel. We specify provenance-binding as the constitutive constraint on the model's outputs: every judgment must resolve to a citation into a fixed canonical corpus, and a judgment that cannot be so resolved is withheld rather than emitted. This trades coverage for auditability deliberately, and it distinguishes the artifact from values models trained on preference data whose sources cannot be named, and from purpose-authored value-rule corpora, whose rules are written for the alignment task itself and therefore cannot serve as an independent ground truth. Finally we specify that a single such artifact bears three non-interchangeable relations to the systems it judges, selected by carrier: a gate in the publisher's own hardware, a citation requirement without veto in an autonomous successor agent, and a referee in the wider world. We state plainly that the middle case must not be implemented as the first, because a veto held by a smaller model over a more capable agent bounds that agent at the evaluator's ceiling — the weak-supervisor problem applied to the very system the arrangement exists to enable. items.summary: This repository contains the code and numerical data supporting the manuscript “Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures” by Juan J. Segura. The study investigates how much relational information modular system interfaces must preserve in order to reconstruct an integrated dynamic-admissibility relation. The reproducibility package contains Python source code, benchmark configuration files, and CSV datasets and outputs used for the principal computational analyses. The package supports two complementary model layers: (1) a reduced continuous-control model used for exhaustive higher-order project-join analysis and robustness studies, and (2) a synthetic seven-state road-relative vehicle model used as a nonlinear dynamic falsification layer. The principal reproducible results include: complete pairwise reconstruction providing no improvement over unary reconstruction; persistence of this pairwise insufficiency across 27 combinations of numerical resolution, superelevation, and stopping horizon; and a sparse ternary architecture comprising the relations {R, mu, v}, {G, mu, v}, and {mu, v, tau} reproducing the complete third-order reconstruction in all 27 robustness cases. The vehicle parameters are synthetic and are not presented as OEM-calibrated haul-truck data. All admissibility projections are exact only with respect to the computed model relation. The reported discordance measures should not be interpreted as accident probabilities or empirical risk frequencies.
items.title: Code and Data for Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures

items.summary: Graph forecasters for sensor networks are trained in one regime and deployed in others, where sensor coupling and signal frequency content both change. We split this spectral shift into an operator channel and a frequency channel, each with a dimensionless measure. ST-GFM (Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting Model) filters every input step with Chebyshev and bidirectional diffusion filters on one learned, non-symmetric operator and alternates them with per-node temporal attention. For the operator channel we prove Frobenius-norm perturbation bounds for both graph branches, show that the Chebyshev bound is attained to first order, and compute its constant from the trained weights and the measured operator norm: 17.9 on METR-LA and 21.5 on PEMS-BAY. Under random edge dropout the trained layer moves by 2.0% to 3.1% of this bound. Masked Spectral Reconstruction (MSR), a self-supervised loss active in the first 40 epochs, matches the log power spectrum of the encoder output to that of the input. For small log-spectral residuals on unclamped bins it is proportional to an Itakura-Saito divergence to leading order. Removing it raises the 60-minute MAE by 0.30 on METR-LA, close to the 0.33 lost when all three self-supervised losses go. Under one shared evaluation pipeline, the 60-minute MAE of ST-GFM is 3.5% below a retrained STAEformer on METR-LA and 13.0% below it on PEMS-BAY. Its 60-minute MAE is 3.0980.017 on METR-LA (five seeds) and 1.5760.006 on PEMS-BAY (three seeds), the lowest PEMS-BAY MAE among twelve published baselines.
items.title: ST-GFM: Spectral-Temporal Graph Forecasting with Measured Perturbation Bounds and Masked Spectral Reconstruction

items.summary: Reduced-order models (ROMs) learned from trusted numerical simulations enable the real-time simulation of complex physical systems, making computationally prohibitive tasks-such as uncertainty quantification and optimal control-tractable. In particular, data-driven ROMs are opening the opportunity to learn from both numerical simulations and experimental data. However, integrating these sources of information is far from straightforward. Real-world measurements often involve multiple sources of uncertainty, including non-Gaussian noise, latent heterogeneities, unknown or hidden system parameters, and multiscale phenomena occurring below the resolution of the data. Consequently, real-world data are better described by parametrized stochastic partial differential equations, for which the development of effective ROMs remains relatively unexplored. In this work, we introduce POD-CNF, a data-driven generative ROM for efficient uncertainty quantification of parametrized high-dimensional systems. The approach combines projection-based model reduction and deep generative modeling. First, Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) is employed to obtain a low-dimensional representation of the solution manifold. A Conditional Normalizing Flow (CNF) is then trained to approximate the density of the reduced coefficients conditionally on the input parameters. This formulation allows the surrogate to capture complex, multimodal output distributions, going beyond standard regression-based ROMs and least-squares predictions. We assess the effectiveness of POD-CNF through numerical experiments, demonstrating its ability to accurately reproduce output distributions while substantially reducing computational costs. Finally, a proof-of-concept application illustrates how the generative paradigm facilitates integration into Bayesian inverse problems, highlighting promising directions for future research.
items.title: POD-CNF: reduced order modeling of parametrized stochastic PDEs via normalizing flows and proper orthogonal decomposition

items.summary: Manuscript and CSV data behind the figures and tables of Xu (2024), On the statistical theory of self-gravitating collisionless dark matter flow: High order kinematic and dynamic relations , Physics of Fluids 36, 075146, doi:10.1063/5.0215026 , arXiv:2202.02991 . Contents: the revised manuscript (PDF) and the CSV files of every plotted series and table, in the format of the author's dark matter flow datasets. Pair statistics from the Virgo SCDM N-body simulation at redshifts z = 10 to 0. Companion datasets: Part I (halo-based) doi:10.5281/zenodo.6541231 , Part II (correlation-based) doi:10.5281/zenodo.6757654 . Major findings (Virgo SCDM N-body simulation, redshifts z = 10 to 0): Kinematic relations of any order are derived for incompressible, constant-divergence and irrotational flow, and validated by the simulation. On large scales, third-order velocity correlations can be related to the density correlation or the pairwise velocity. The p-th order velocity correlations follow a^((p+2)/2) for odd p and a^(p/2) for even p (a = scale factor). The fitted exponents for odd p are smaller than these predictions. The overdensity is proportional to the density correlation on the same scale, <delta> ∝ <delta delta'>; the velocity dispersion on a scale r is proportional to the overdensity on that scale. The effective viscosity of the adhesion model originates from velocity fluctuations; the negative viscosity is due to the inverse energy cascade. On small scales, a self-closed velocity evolution is obtained by splitting velocity into motion within haloes and motion of haloes. Vorticity, enstrophy and energy evolution follow from it. The mean pairwise velocity follows <Δu_L> = −H a r. The third moment follows <(Δu_L)^3> ∝ ε_u a r, with a constant energy-cascade rate ε_u ≈ −4.6×10⁻⁷ m²/s³. The combined kinematic and dynamic relations give exponential velocity correlations on large scales and one-fourth power-law correlations on small scales; the p-th order correlations follow a^((3p−5)/4) for odd p and a^(3p/4) for even p.

items.summary: We develop nonreciprocal spherical attention as a mathematical framework for coarsening and compressed nearest-neighbor retrieval. For two shrinking acute blocks whose centers have zero skew pairing and whose total mass ratio is subexponential in inverse temperature, we prove $\lim_{β\to\infty}β^{-1}\log T_β=1-\cosφ$, without restricting particle-count growth. An explicit three-body flow has two rigorously separated metastable exponents. For finite compression, mass centering yields a sharp $O(r^2)$ attention-output error bound at fixed temperature, with an explicit spherical-normalization correction. We formulate skew query-side score calibration as a strictly convex moment problem and derive a unique normal equation, residual-based optimization certificates, and bounded low-rank projections. A norm-aware margin objective calibrates native squared-distance rankings. Experiments use semantic retrieval data, one million visual descriptors with three codebook seeds, and a ten-million-vector FAISS IVF-PQ index with recomputed exact cosine ground truth. On SIFT1M, skew margin calibration raises native-L2 hit@10 from 0.8926 to 0.8948; symmetric calibration reaches 0.8996. The ten-million-vector index reaches 0.8827 hit@10 at 0.1794 ms per query in a four-thread batch benchmark, while validation selects no skew update. Exact streamed attention over ten million keys evaluates compressed memory on 1,024 held-out queries. Independent matrix solves, automatic differentiation, finite differences, interval arithmetic, full-flow tests, and nine Rocq-checked algebra lemmas support reproducibility. Directionality alone does not establish retrieval superiority.
items.title: Nonreciprocal Spherical Attention and Retrieval: Sharp Coarsening Clocks and Certified Score Correction

items.summary: Classical creative-process orderings put divergence early and convergence late, and the Double Diamond formalises the rule twice over. This paper argues the ordering was never a law of cognition but a map of costs: divergence goes early because reopening a converged process has historically been ruinous, and the entire discipline of the framework exists to protect against that reopening. When drafting cost collapses by orders of magnitude, as it does when an author works with a language model as typewriter, the protected assumption dissolves and the optimal ordering inverts: converge first, then diverge, because a late horizon either restarts a now-cheap process or spawns a child concept from a sharpened parent. The paper's second claim types reviewer instances in multi-model chains by regression target rather than capability, and states the Hein Condition: a mode-regressing reviewer's yield is proportional to the sharpness of the artefact it receives, because the modal response to an unsharp artefact is the generic response, so the same instance is most fluent exactly where it is least useful. A slot theory follows, carnivore, auditor, mode-regressor, children, each reviewer placed where its failure mode is cheapest, and child viability rises with parent sharpness at spawn. The claims are exercised on a fully documented case: a five-pass, three-model review chain run on a single paper in a single day, with every absorption, declination, and provenance failure logged. Four predictions close, including that review chains are provenance systems measurable by the sibling paper's key-inflation ratio.

items.summary: Measured failure modes of verifier panels: companion paper accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? — Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels . Version of record: SSRN 7390698 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7390698 . Cite that version. The same text is also at https://polyhelper.ai/research/agreement-not-evidence/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/agreement-not-evidence . Someone who asks one language model a question cannot tell a confidently wrong answer from a confidently right one. The two are identical on every surface cue available to a non-expert. Asking several models seems to solve this, but it mostly relocates the problem: reconciling several answers produces one confident text again, and that text now carries the borrowed authority of "ten of them agreed." The protocol formalized here collects answers from several consumer chat models through the user's own browser or phone, with no API keys, no installation and no intermediary server. It reconciles them by anchor-and-enrich: the strongest available answer becomes the base, and each of the others contributes only what the base lacks. Every contribution is signed with the model that supplied it. Disagreements are kept in a section of their own rather than averaged away. The paper makes four contributions. The first is the protocol itself, stated as an algorithm that preserves provenance and forbids silent deletion, together with a taxonomy of five ways a merge can fail. Four of them are defects of naive pooling; the fifth is a failure of the operator rather than of the method: a synthesis that presents a single model's output as a collegial result. The second is the application of the correlated-witness arithmetic to protocol design. That arithmetic is not claimed here. Kohli (2026) applied the same Kish correction to a panel of nine frontier judges and measured about two effective votes, and Kim et al. (2025) established the underlying error correlation across more than 350 models. A council of N models whose errors carry intraclass correlation ρ is worth = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ) independent witnesses, and that quantity saturates at 1/ρ however many models are added. Once a council is larger than 1/ρ, halving ρ beats doubling N, and a pair with low error correlation can outweigh five with high correlation. Which pairs those are is measured, not read off the label: the larger and more accurate models carry the most correlated errors even when architecture and provider differ (Kim et al., 2025), and the author's per-pair measurements found no detectable effect of geopolitical bloc on error correlation and, in the pairs measured, none of shared lineage (Chernets, 2026). The estimation procedure of Section 5.5 supplies that measurement. The third is an account of three deployment tiers, manual, one-tap mobile and browser-agent, and of the axis that separates them epistemically: whether the second model sees the first model's answer. Conditioning the second model raises ρ in exchange for error correction. The fourth is a small-sample observation of the counterfeit-council failure across five models, the one-sentence intervention that removed it in a three-model re-run, and a blinded three-arm evaluation design with a stated falsification condition. Correlated agreement is treated here as established, not as a finding. That a panel of models is worth far fewer independent witnesses than it has members has been measured directly: nine frontier judges drawn from seven families supply about two effective votes (Kohli, 2026), and error correlation rises with model capability even across providers and architectures (Kim et al., 2025). Section 5 restates the design-effect arithmetic behind those measurements, because three of the protocol's rules are derived from it and read as fastidiousness without it. items.summary: Measured failure modes of verifier panels: companion paper accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 workshop Who Verifies the Agents? — Verification Theater: Measured Failure Modes of AI Verifier Panels . Version of record: SSRN 7390698 , DOI 10.2139/ssrn.7390698 . Cite that version. The same text is also at https://polyhelper.ai/research/agreement-not-evidence/ and https://github.com/vadimchernets/papers/tree/main/agreement-not-evidence . Someone who asks one language model a question cannot tell a confidently wrong answer from a confidently right one. The two are identical on every surface cue available to a non-expert. Asking several models seems to solve this, but it mostly relocates the problem: reconciling several answers produces one confident text again, and that text now carries the borrowed authority of "ten of them agreed." The protocol formalized here collects answers from several consumer chat models through the user's own browser or phone, with no API keys, no installation and no intermediary server. It reconciles them by anchor-and-enrich: the strongest available answer becomes the base, and each of the others contributes only what the base lacks. Every contribution is signed with the model that supplied it. Disagreements are kept in a section of their own rather than averaged away. The paper makes four contributions. The first is the protocol itself, stated as an algorithm that preserves provenance and forbids silent deletion, together with a taxonomy of five ways a merge can fail. Four of them are defects of naive pooling; the fifth is a failure of the operator rather than of the method: a synthesis that presents a single model's output as a collegial result. The second is the application of the correlated-witness arithmetic to protocol design. That arithmetic is not claimed here. Kohli (2026) applied the same Kish correction to a panel of nine frontier judges and measured about two effective votes, and Kim et al. (2025) established the underlying error correlation across more than 350 models. A council of N models whose errors carry intraclass correlation ρ is worth = N / (1 + (N−1)ρ) independent witnesses, and that quantity saturates at 1/ρ however many models are added. Once a council is larger than 1/ρ, halving ρ beats doubling N, and a pair with low error correlation can outweigh five with high correlation. Which pairs those are is measured, not read off the label: the larger and more accurate models carry the most correlated errors even when architecture and provider differ (Kim et al., 2025), and the author's per-pair measurements found no detectable effect of geopolitical bloc on error correlation and, in the pairs measured, none of shared lineage (Chernets, 2026). The estimation procedure of Section 5.5 supplies that measurement. The third is an account of three deployment tiers, manual, one-tap mobile and browser-agent, and of the axis that separates them epistemically: whether the second model sees the first model's answer. Conditioning the second model raises ρ in exchange for error correction. Correlated agreement is treated here as established, not as a finding. Section 5 restates the design-effect arithmetic behind those measurements, because three of the protocol's rules are derived from it and read as fastidiousness without it. items.summary: Sensor fusion, data fusion, dashboards and data visualisation are conventionally distinguished by input type and by where they sit in a processing stack. This paper argues that the distinction which matters for decision quality is a different one, and that it is two variables applied to all four: every representation of multi-source evidence collapses a distribution somewhere between sensor and decision, and representations differ in the locus of that collapse and in whether the residual uncertainty survives it as a carried object. Fusion collapses upstream and, when honest, ships the residual as covariance or hypothesis mass. Dashboards defer collapse to the viewer's retina and ship nothing; the resulting belief has no bookkeeping. Visualisation is the encoding of whichever object arrives, indifferent to whether it is a point or a distribution, which is why it is blamed for collapses committed upstream. The two variables, collapse locus and residual retention, place the four terms on one map, generalise the confabulation coefficient of The Confabulating Collator from language-model collators to the whole representation stack, and yield a diagnostic: the failure mode conventionally called bad fusion is a product that collapsed upstream and discarded its residual, delivering the confidence of a posterior with the epistemic hygiene of a gauge. The publicly reported expectation, in the investigation of the February 2026 Minab strike, that a targeting platform would have flagged contradictions it carried no representation of, is read as this failure at operational scale, with the causal question left where the public record leaves it. A design rule follows: defer collapse to the human where the human carries the prior the system lacks, fuse where they do not, and at neither locus discard the residual. The constructive requirement for language-level fusion products is stated and handed to a companion paper on divergence retention. The operator located in the architecture is Binary Bias.

items.summary: Version 1.02, 3 November 2026. Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020) estimate that one additional industrial robot per thousand workers lowers a U.S. local labor market's employment-to-population ratio by 0.39 percentage points and its hourly wages by about 0.77 percent. Rebuilding their design from raw IPUMS, IFR, and EU KLEMS data, I reproduce these estimates bit-exactly. I then ask what conventional robustness checks leave open: which industries, places, periods, and shocks actually identify the estimate? The regression spans 722 commuting zones and 19 industries, but the variation behind an instrumental-variable estimate can be far narrower. The sign is robust; the support is narrow. Negative estimates persist across conventional specification changes, 60 strong European instrument windows, alternative U.S. treatment windows, and the published periods through 2014. Yet automotive carries about 84 percent of normalized absolute Rotemberg-weight mass, and automotive exposure in six Rust Belt states supplies 95 percent of the net first-stage covariance. Without automotive, the remaining 18 industry shocks do not strongly predict U.S. robot exposure. Longer horizons, later start years, and adding Germany to the instrument all strengthen it through the same margin. The automotive component shows no detectable relation to 1970–1990 employment and wage changes, and a direct effect of the instrument would have to absorb 72 percent of the reduced form before conventional significance disappears. Inference is weaker than the regional first stage suggests. With 19 underlying industry shocks, exposure-robust first-stage F-statistics are 6.2 and 6.3 rather than 34, small-sample Anderson–Rubin tests do not reject a zero effect ( p = 0.059, 0.063), and other implementations of the same test disagree; in known-truth simulations, nominal 95-percent state-clustered intervals cover in only 60–66 percent of replications. Measurement assumptions also bind. In the original penetration metric, perpetual-inventory robot capital preserves the estimates at 5 percent depreciation, but faster assumed depreciation counts the automotive installations behind the first stage as replacement rather than net additions, eliminating shock-level relevance at 10 percent and all relevance at 15 percent. The benchmark is reproducible and robust in sign, but it is identified from an automotive margin in historically industrial labor markets; that margin defines its scope and the concrete content of its exclusion restriction. More generally, coefficient robustness and breadth of identifying support are distinct properties that shift-share studies should report separately. items.title: Robots and Jobs Revisited: A Bit-Exact Replication, Shift-Share Anatomy, and Capital-Stock Extension of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020)

items.summary: Progress in robot learning, particularly physical multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), is currently challenged by a limited availability of accessible, standardized benchmarks. While simulation-based MARL has produced remarkable emergent behaviors, from coordinated team play to complex tool use, translating these advances to physical systems remains difficult. A key barrier is infrastructural: physical platforms are often prohibitively expensive, require specialized facilities, or lack open mechanisms and designs for reproducibility. We introduce KlaskTron, an open-source, low-cost (<\$2500 USD), desktop-scale robotic testbed for adversarial MARL based on the dynamic tabletop game KLASK. The platform features dual CoreXY gantries with high-torque brushless motors, enabling the high-speed, precise manipulation required for competitive play. Crucially, we provide a complete ecosystem: hardware designs (CAD, BOM), a GPU-native digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Lab for high-fidelity modeling and simulation, and a validated sim-to-real baseline using a learned neural actuator model. We demonstrate that this baseline enables zero-shot policy transfer, with trained agents exhibiting emergent adversarial behaviors. To ensure full reproducibility of our results, all project assets are released publicly: hardware CAD/BOM and assembly documentation at [https://idscethzurich.github.io/klask_hardware], inference software stack at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_software] and the simulation and MARL setup at [https://github.com/IDSCETHZurich/klask_rl].
items.title: KlaskTron: An Open-Source Platform for Physical Adversarial Multi-Agent RL

items.summary: This repository contains the code and numerical data supporting the manuscript “Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures” by Juan J. Segura. The study investigates how much relational information modular system interfaces must preserve in order to reconstruct an integrated dynamic-admissibility relation. The reproducibility package contains Python source code, benchmark configuration files, and CSV datasets and outputs used for the principal computational analyses. The package supports two complementary model layers: (1) a reduced continuous-control model used for exhaustive higher-order project-join analysis and robustness studies, and (2) a synthetic seven-state road-relative vehicle model used as a nonlinear dynamic falsification layer. The principal reproducible results include: complete pairwise reconstruction providing no improvement over unary reconstruction; persistence of this pairwise insufficiency across 27 combinations of numerical resolution, superelevation, and stopping horizon; and a sparse ternary architecture comprising the relations {R, mu, v}, {G, mu, v}, and {mu, v, tau} reproducing the complete third-order reconstruction in all 27 robustness cases. The vehicle parameters are synthetic and are not presented as OEM-calibrated haul-truck data. All admissibility projections are exact only with respect to the computed model relation. The reported discordance measures should not be interpreted as accident probabilities or empirical risk frequencies.
items.title: Code and Data for Higher-Order Relational Assurance for Modular Autonomous System Architectures

items.summary: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization has emerged as a promising approach for memory-efficient large language model (LLM) post-training, yet its reliable application to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) remains largely unexplored. Motivated by the distinct data regimes of on-policy RL and fixed-data optimization, we develop a generic variance-theoretic framework to investigate what limits the reliability of ZO gradient estimation. Our analysis reveals that estimation reliability is structurally determined by whether the two finite-difference evaluations are performed on matched data. On-policy reinforcement learning (RL) under the mismatched-data regime produces a $1/μ^2$ oracle-noise amplification that sets an irreducible noise floor as the perturbation scale $μ$ decreases, whereas Boltzmann Targeted SFT (BOLT) under the matched-data regime eliminates this amplification via noise cancellation. We further derive convergence guarantees with explicit constants that cleanly separate the two regimes. These results naturally lead to ZO-BOLT, which applies ZO optimization to BOLT's RLVR-aligned weighted-SFT objective. Controlled perturbation-scale sweeps and matched-versus-mismatched end-to-end comparisons validate the predicted effect of data matching. Experiments across three model variants and two mathematical reasoning benchmarks further show that ZO-BOLT consistently improves over the pretrained baseline while retaining a near-inference memory footprint. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/lianmin-chen/the_cost_of_mismatch.
items.title: The Cost of Mismatch: Noise Amplification in Zeroth-Order Reinforcement Learning

items.summary: Optimal control of partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs), in general, requires a complete history. The belief state, a distribution over hidden states, summarizes this history and provides the classical sufficient statistic to control POMDPs. However, the continuous nature of the belief space generally prevents a finite-memory controller from maintaining it exactly. This raises the question we address in this work: what must the available finite memory preserve to achieve near-optimal control performance? We study this question through an information-theoretic converse that gives a fundamental lower bound on the loss of any finite-memory controller. The analysis introduces the concept of a decision witness that characterizes belief states whose confusion would lead to unavoidable loss. Motivated by this bound, we propose RECAP, a constructive quantization method for designing representative memory states. We prove an upper bound on the optimality gap of any RECAP codebook and use the components of this bound together with the converse analysis to define the codebook objective. Experiments on 11 POMDP benchmarks demonstrate that RECAP improves over finite-memory representation baselines under the same memory budget.
items.title: Finite-Memory Control of POMDPs: Fundamental Limits and Efficient Design

items.summary: Visual mental imagery (VMI) decoding uses brain activity to reconstruct internally generated visual scenes, providing a potential pathway for externalizing internal experiences and developing neuroprosthetic communication interfaces. However, progress is limited by the lack of dedicated, training-scale VMI datasets. Current VMI paradigms often rely on visual prompts or short-term memory images, introducing visual and mnemonic confounds that make it difficult to disentangle neural activity associated with endogenous image construction from signals driven by prior or concurrent visual input. Furthermore, existing VMI datasets offer limited descriptive control over individual visual attributes, making it difficult to systematically assess fine grained visual details. To address these gaps, we introduce AVID, the first dedicated training-scale 5.0 Tesla functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) resource for auditory-induced VMI decoding. AVID comprises approximately 67 hours of dense recordings from nine participants. The dataset is structured into two complementary splits: a scene-level complex split using naturalistic Mandarin descriptions and a controlled simple split with explicitly specified visual attributes. We further formalize a standardized evaluation protocol that decouples source-image consistency from semantic alignment, allowing for a more nuanced assessment of imagery reconstruction. Baseline qualitative and quantitative results show that current reconstruction pipelines remain limited on AVID, although the most successful reconstructions preserve recognizable scene level semantics from spoken descriptions. By combining dedicated training-scale neural recordings and standardized evaluation resources, AVID provides both a data foundation for imagery-specific model development and a benchmark for evaluating VMI decoding with substantially reduced sensory contamination.
items.title: AVID: A 5T fMRI Dataset for Benchmarking Auditory-induced Visual Mental Imagery Decoding
